# Decisions And Constraints

<!-- Generated by repo-harness-builder; source: core/docs:3.0 -->

## Standing Decisions
<!-- doc-role:standing-decisions -->

- Repository documentation remains the visible source of project state.
- Gentle AI and Engram are required for integrated continuity, but never override current repository evidence.
- Editable product sources are `skill/repo-harness-builder/` and `command/repo-harness-builder.md`; `.opencode/` and `.claude/` are runtime projections for execution and testing.
- This repository recursively uses its generated harness to improve the builder itself.
- Git initialization and provider publication are optional, separately approved boundaries. Publication also requires an explicit private or public visibility choice.
- New or effectively empty repositories receive a complete useful baseline after plan approval, including `README.md`. Existing repositories receive content analysis and an informed integration proposal. Obsolete or incompatible content may be archived for a clean baseline only after a distinct conversational choice and explicit approval.
- Generated ownership markers may bound generated material but never exempt a pre-existing README or other human-owned document from analysis and improvement.
- Only builder apply uses strict language-scoped digest-bound tokens: English `APPROVE` or `DENY`, Spanish `APROBAR` or `DENEGAR`. Apply requires both digest and exact token. Direct CLI calls default to English, language never enters the plan digest, and generated session skills remain conversational.
- Root runtime pointers preserve all existing bytes, detect the exact directive as a complete line, and append only the missing newline-delimited directive using the existing consistent line-ending convention where possible.
- Prior harness versions are audited rather than refused because managed files exist. Upgrade analysis classifies current, stale, missing, human-evolved, and legacy paths. Replacement, archive, and deletion require an exact proposed action and explicit user approval.
- Generated session-stop approvals are resumable checkpoints within the same invocation. Approved actions run once, declined documentation does not stop closing, and final handoff output follows refreshed evidence and successful final continuity saving.
- Generated session-start synchronizes only after read-only state inspection and conversational outcome approval. Explicit safe-sync intent covers bounded fetch and fast-forward-only integration while facts remain unchanged, never blind pull, rebase, reset, or automatic conflict resolution.
- Generated session-stop completes documentation and continuity before Git. Consent is outcome-scoped: combined commit-and-push intent covers exact staging, one read-only staged-scope check, commit, checks, one fetch preflight, and one push to the identified upstream. The staged check compares workflow path names and status/modes with the approved work unit while keeping pre-existing staged work separate. A mismatch invalidates consent; selective unstage is allowed only when it cannot disturb pre-existing staged work. Commit-only and push-only stay narrow. Material scope, sensitivity, remote, destination, credential, integration, hook, or verification changes invalidate consent.
- Generated sessions use scoped `ready`, `paused`, `blocked`, `failed`, `completed`, and `degraded` outcomes. Required continuity and optional Git branches report separately, and optional Git failure never falsely fails the whole session.
- Every safe pending approval is one concrete final question. Commit proposals require per-path sensitive screening, exact work-unit paths, rationale, Conventional Commit message, exclusions, and staged-path disclosure. Transport diagnostics retain bounded command receipts and safely-local state.
- Self-hosted verification separates on-disk projection parity from active-process registered skill freshness and from runtime reload capability. Same-process stale registered content degrades only optional live validation; it does not block or fail verified repository state, documentation close, or continuity, and no reload command is assumed.
- Spanish generated docs use complete natural templates rather than chained heading replacement. The checker combines locale-independent semantic roles with proportional required-phrase and known-leakage baselines; it detects missing required content but does not pretend automated checks prove semantic equivalence.
- Declared documentation locales and the conversation language control generated runtime help routing, so the help wrapper can only name a guide the same render creates. The report language is presentational and changes no generated byte, so the action-plan digest stays identical across report languages with no normalization.
- README selector integration is atomic. When an existing `README.md` lacks the reciprocal Spanish link and no approved existing-file integration action is executable, `README.es.md` is blocked and the whole apply fails closed. Executable existing-file integration remains a broader pending capability.
- Repository contributions are issue-first, use short focused branches and linked PRs, follow Conventional Commits, keep tests and docs in the same work unit, and require maintainer review before merge. Direct changes to `main` require an explicit maintainer emergency; approval is conversational because this repository has no custom contribution labels, templates, or automated approval gate.
